## Critique
- claim-1: The computation is exact and successfully executed. It reconstructs the complete Pieri rows, verifies all sixteen degree-\(10\) supports have \(\phi\)-value \(0\), and uses the accepted Smith data correctly: invariant factors all \(1\) make the rank-\(11\) relation lattice saturated; since \(\phi\) is primitive, \(\ker\phi\) is also saturated of rank \(11\), so containment implies equality. Thus \(e_{22222}-e_{442}\in\ker\phi\), giving \(T_{10}=(1)\). The reported blocks, determinants, Smith diagonals, and global witness \(U=T,\ V=I_6,\ UTV=I_6\) are consistent. However, the specialist output does not explicitly state the transition convention, the dominance-unitriangularity verdict, or whether the requested target is established.
- claim-2: Correctly identifies a failed execution as supplying no positive evidence; it is irrelevant to the successful replacement certificate.
- claim-3: Correctly limits the finite computation to this specialization and avoids asserting the parent theorem.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] In the convention
  \[
  [g_{L,r}]=\sum_c(T_d)_{r,c}[g_{R,c}],
  \]
  with degreewise orders
  \[
  \begin{array}{c|c|c}
  d&G_L&G_R\\\hline
  6&(222)&(222)\\
  7&(2221)&(322)\\
  8&(2222,22211)&(422,332)\\
  9&(22221)&(432)\\
  10&(22222)&(442),
  \end{array}
  \]
  the transition is not dominance-unitriangular: \(T_8=\begin{psmallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{psmallmatrix}\) is not triangular in the displayed dominance-descending orders, while \(T_7=T_9=(-1)\) have diagonal entry \(-1\), not \(1\).

## Required revisions
- State the convention and degreewise \(G_L,G_R\) orders explicitly.
- State explicitly:
  \[
  T_6=(1),\quad T_7=(-1),\quad
  T_8=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
  T_9=(-1),\quad T_{10}=(1),
  \]
  and that the requested bounded certificate is established.
- Include the explicit negative dominance-unitriangularity conclusion above. Do not claim the parent theorem.
